# Story Package: The Last Supper & Washing the Disciples’ Feet (John 13, Matthew 26, Mark 14, Luke 22)

**Story Key**: `lastSupper`

**Position in 365 Roadmap**: Phase 6, Story #25 — Jesus shows us what true love and servant-heartedness look like.

---

## Reverent Read-Aloud Retelling (for ages 3–8)

It was the night before Jesus would go to the cross. He and His twelve disciples gathered in a quiet upstairs room to eat the Passover meal together. This would be their last supper before everything changed.

During the meal, Jesus did something very surprising. He got up from the table, took off His outer robe, wrapped a towel around His waist, and poured water into a basin. Then He began to wash His disciples’ dirty feet and dry them with the towel.

Peter was shocked. “Lord, are You going to wash my feet?” he asked.

Jesus answered, “You do not realize now what I am doing, but later you will understand.”

When He had finished, Jesus said, “Do you understand what I have done for you? You call Me ‘Teacher’ and ‘Lord,’ and rightly so, for that is what I am. Now that I, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also should wash one another’s feet. I have set you an example that you should do as I have done for you.”

Then Jesus took bread, gave thanks, broke it, and gave it to them. “This is My body given for you,” He said. He also took the cup and said, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood, which is poured out for you.”

He told them, “A new command I give you: Love one another. As I have loved you, so you must love one another. By this everyone will know that you are My disciples, if you love one another.”

---

## Coloring Page Prompt

Simple, reverent black-and-white line art for ages 3–8. Jesus kneeling and gently washing a disciple’s feet with a towel. Other disciples sitting around a low table with bread and cups. Soft lamplight. Peaceful, humble, and loving feeling. Clean bold lines with large open spaces.

---

## Read-Along Flow

Color Jesus washing feet and sharing the bread and cup → listen to His new command to love one another the way He loves us → remember that the greatest love serves others and gives itself away. Perfect for teaching kindness and humility any day.

## Quiz — 4 Questions (with helpful scaffolding)

**1. What surprising thing did Jesus do during the meal?**
- A) He told everyone to go home
- B) He got up and washed His disciples’ dirty feet
- C) He asked the disciples to wash His feet first
- D) He ate all the food by Himself

*Correct: B*  
Wrong answers scaffolding:
- If A: “Jesus stayed and did something very humble. He washed their feet to show them what real love looks like.”
- If C: “He served them instead of asking them to serve Him first. That was the surprise.”
- If D: “He shared the meal with them and used it to teach them about love and sacrifice.”

**2. Why did Peter not want Jesus to wash his feet at first?**
- A) Because his feet were already clean
- B) Because he thought it was too lowly a job for Jesus, his Lord and Teacher
- C) Because he didn’t like water
- D) Because he wanted to wash Jesus’ feet instead

*Correct: B*  
Wrong answers scaffolding:
- If A: “His feet were dusty from walking. Peter’s surprise was that the Lord would do such a humble task.”
- If C: “It wasn’t about the water. Peter felt Jesus was too important to wash feet.”
- If D: “He eventually let Jesus wash his feet after Jesus explained it was an example of love.”

**3. What new command did Jesus give His disciples that night?**
- A) “Never eat bread again”
- B) “Love one another. As I have loved you, so you must love one another.”
- C) “Only wash each other’s feet on special days”
- D) “Make sure everyone knows you are the smartest”

*Correct: B*  
Wrong answers scaffolding:
- If A: “He used the bread to help them remember Him, but the new command was about loving each other the way He loves us.”
- If C: “The foot washing was an example of humble love. The command was to keep loving one another every day.”
- If D: “Jesus wanted them to be known by their love, not by how important they seemed.”

**4. What does the bread and the cup help us remember?**
- A) That Jesus likes big parties
- B) That Jesus gave His body and poured out His blood for us
- C) That we should only eat bread and drink juice
- D) That the disciples were very hungry

*Correct: B*  
Wrong answers scaffolding:
- If A: “It’s not about the party. The bread and cup are a way to remember Jesus’ great love and sacrifice for us.”
- If C: “We do share the Lord’s Supper to remember, but the most important thing is what it points to — Jesus giving Himself for us.”
- If D: “The meal was special because of what Jesus said about His body and blood, not just because they were eating.”
